target_work.title: How should a luxury fashion house read the current research on sustainability, legitimacy and brand activism before maki
target_work.description: The research draws a clear line between sustainability commitments that stick and those that invite backlash—and the dividing variable is not ambition, it is coherence. U3PWD6J3 shows that consumers accept brand activism only when they can trace a logical thread from the brand's history to the cause it champions; WUPV36YG shows that even a well-received public gesture collapses when internal governance contradicts the message. For a luxury house, this means the sequence matters as much as the substance: governance and sourcing decisions must precede the press release, not follow it. SG4IGV3Y adds the structural warning that any commitment framed purely as market opportunity will be read—correctly—as neoliberal co-optation. research_question: Before You Commit: The Legitimacy Gap Diagnostic
strategy_summary: The angle is diagnostic and action-oriented: executives need to know (1) what the legitimacy threshold actually is across the literature, and (2) where and why commitments collapse. Phase 1 uses concept_centrality_mapper to convert scattered theoretical claims into a unified map of legitimacy conditions—essentially the "pass/fail" criteria the executive checklist requires. Phase 2 uses dialectical_structure to animate that map by showing the underlying market-vs.-civic tension that generates each failure mode; this transforms a static list into a causal story about why sequencing (governance before announcement) is not optional. Each phase feeds the next: the concept map gives the dialectical analysis its vocabulary and its stakes, while the dialectical analysis gives the concept map its explanatory power. Both are held at surface depth, consistent with the medium corpus policy and the executive audience's need for sharp conclusions over exhaustive exposition.

phases.context_emphasis: Focus squarely on 'legitimacy' and its satellite concepts (coherence, heritage link, governance alignment, opportunism, co-optation) as they appear in U3PWD6J3, WUPV36YG, and SG4IGV3Y. Map what each document treats as necessary vs. merely sufficient conditions; this inventory becomes the raw material for the dialectical phase.
phases.rationale: Legitimacy is the load-bearing concept the angle explicitly identifies as the diagnostic variable. This engine will map, across all five documents, precisely what conditions each source says must be satisfied before legitimacy is granted—turning theoretical claims into a structured checklist of pre-conditions. It establishes the shared conceptual skeleton that the second phase will stress-test.

phases.context_emphasis: The prior phase established the legitimacy conditions per document. Build on that by identifying the market-world vs. civic-world contradiction as the master dialectic, tracing how U3PWD6J3's Economies of Worth framework, WUPV36YG's governance gap, and SG4IGV3Y's neoliberal co-optation warning each represent a different moment of the same tension—and what resolution each document implies for a luxury brand's communication sequence.
phases.rationale: The angle's core insight is a structural tension—market-world interest vs. civic-world obligation—that explains every failure mode named in the brief. After the concept map establishes what legitimacy requires, this engine surfaces how each document works out that contradiction, revealing exactly where a luxury brand's commitment is most exposed and what sequence of moves (governance before press release) defuses the challenge.
